correctness.rationale: The finite-level gauge lemma and its converse are explicit; the exact loop product changes by p-th powers under refinement. At high level the p-primary component is annihilated, giving the normalized p-regular constant h; uniqueness follows from invertibility of prime powers modulo p-regular orders. The Chinese remainder theorem proves clopen minimal components and local return groups for all finite G, without relying on experiments. The 3250 finite diagnostics check group order, refinement, cycle counts, cycle lengths and gauge criteria; they do not prove the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: A full natural classification of all continuous finite-group cocycles over a prime-adic adding machine, as opposed to an isolated normalization check, is useful for determining whether extensions are equivalent and how their minimal components split. Explicitly, over the dyadic odometer with C7, all six nonidentity constants have the same single-component dynamics but represent different gauge cohomology classes, demonstrating nonredundant resolution. The modular representation count identifies the size of the classification with a standard finite-group invariant. The exact class invariant and all-component odometer type hold for every finite (including nonabelian) group, without a downstream theorem being required.
